verdict: The two named helper fixes and corner clarification are correct, but the executable parser dependency closure is still incomplete. M2227 remains unconsumed and must not run under this source identity.

findings.name: Unconditional second-level M2160 import bypasses the source identity gate
findings.evidence: M2217 parser imports M2172, whose BASE = load_base() unconditionally calls exec_module on parse_m2160_m2018_ordinary_native_saif_report_reset_preflight.py. M2160 is absent from the 28-member source_inventory and is never hashed by source_validation. Neither M2160 nor its caller validates the M2160 SHA before execution.
findings.reproduction: The independent CPU-only review traces the real import chain. An in-memory replacement loader for only M2160 then proves source_validation(False) passes before the unbound module executes and raises the injected marker. No production source file was modified.
findings.impact: A changed M2160 file executes after the frozen source gate. The current M2217 production parser does not call BASE.audit_single_axis_source, so the current defect is unbound import-time executable code rather than evidence that today's power arithmetic is already wrong. It nevertheless violates the stated complete production source identity and can alter or interrupt parser execution.
findings.remediation: Create a successor source identity that pins the complete local executable import closure, including M2160 SHA 381fbaac6c75aed86aa1dd12aad41dffeb8348c7a875e95f1c162256df6ba22b. Bind every helper in inventory, preflight, source review identity and result identity, and test all helper mutations before EDA. M2160 and M2117 themselves import only Python standard-library modules; no further project-local helper was found. Re-review independently before a fresh sole attempt.
